subject: Environmental Studies
stem: A frog spends its early life (as a tadpole) breathing through gills in water, then develops lungs and legs to live on land as an adult, though it must return to water to lay eggs. This class of animals, able to live both in water and on land, is called:
explanation: Amphibians (frogs, toads, salamanders) undergo metamorphosis from an aquatic, gill-breathing larval stage to a land-capable, lung-breathing adult stage — distinct from reptiles, which are born with lungs and do not require water for reproduction (mostly laying eggs on land).
